cases.title: Sidewalk Toronto / Quayside
cases.domain: urban development, data governance, public-private partnership
cases.research_role: hard case for standing, public authority and data rights
cases.case_selection_rationale: A bilateral development relation proposed rules with public externalities; it reveals when parties to a contract are not the only entities with legitimate standing.

initial_relation_frame.R: Waterfront Toronto, Sidewalk Labs, three levels of government, expert panel, public/affected communities, future development partners.
initial_relation_frame.V: Master plan, land development, digital proposals, data governance, public benefit, IP, approvals.
initial_relation_frame.T: Proposal → consultation/evaluation → threshold resolution → board/government approvals or refusal → implementation agreements or termination.
initial_relation_frame.A: Waterfront Toronto and Sidewalk approvals; public-sector/government authority over privacy, digital governance and land/public-interest decisions.
initial_relation_frame.E: Public consultation, technical evaluation, expert review, legal/regulatory compliance and future project readbacks.
initial_relation_frame.D: Collection, localization, governance, use and public value of urban data; IP and co-created assets.
initial_relation_frame.O: Pursue all/some/none; staged approvals; implementation agreements; withdrawal/termination.

powers: law, land, planning, privacy and regulatory approvals
standing to challenge and shape public-interest evaluation; not identical to bilateral signature authority
independent expert challenge/advice; no final approval

timeline.label: Plan Development Agreement creates a staged relation
timeline.description: The agreement defines the parties, approvals, development process and multiple termination conditions rather than treating the project as a simple purchase.
timeline.authority_effect: Creates bilateral approval and exit authority.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates a formal formation process, not final implementation.

timeline.label: Draft MIDP expands the proposed relation
timeline.description: The draft plan introduces broad land, governance, data, IP and implementation proposals beyond a narrow parameter negotiation.
timeline.authority_effect: Proposes new governance and implementation roles.
timeline.outcome_effect: Starts public/technical evaluation rather than producing acceptance.

timeline.label: Public consultation challenges scope, governance, consent and data proposals
timeline.description: Public feedback objects to scope overreach, unclear democratic control, surveillance/consent, IP and missing public-benefit evidence.
timeline.authority_effect: Demonstrates that affected stakeholders have claims not reducible to the two contracting parties.
timeline.outcome_effect: Requires material reconsideration before approval.

timeline.label: Threshold resolution reallocates authority and constrains data governance
timeline.description: Waterfront Toronto becomes the lead for privacy/digital governance and government discussions; public consultation, Canadian storage and public-sector control replace or constrain parts of the original proposal.
timeline.authority_effect: Moves key governance authority away from the private proposer and requires broader approval.
timeline.outcome_effect: Produces a narrower, conditionally viable relation version.

timeline.label: Expert panel accepts improvement but finds critical details unresolved
timeline.description: The expert review reports that the revised appendix is materially improved while a fully realized digital-governance framework and other critical details remain absent.
timeline.authority_effect: Blocks silent conversion of a partial resolution into public acceptance.
timeline.outcome_effect: Keeps the relation in conditional/unknown state.

timeline.label: Sidewalk Labs terminates the PDA
timeline.description: The contractual relation is terminated. Official reporting attributes withdrawal to unprecedented economic uncertainty arising from COVID-19; governance disputes cannot be asserted as the cause of termination.
timeline.authority_effect: Exercises a valid exit path; surviving IP/data/confidentiality provisions remain.
timeline.outcome_effect: Outcome is WITHDRAWN, not rejected on a proved governance cause.

operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.operation: Extensive plan development, consultation and threshold negotiation occurred; no full project implementation.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.effect: Formal governance/scope terms changed and the development agreement was terminated.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.adoption: Waterfront Toronto reports retaining planning insights; the Quayside proposal itself was not adopted.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.acceptance: No final multi-authority acceptance of the project. Public/expert positions remained heterogeneous.

supports: Material relation change can be driven by authority, standing, data rights and effect rules rather than price or scope alone.
Bilateral recognition is insufficient when third parties bear public externalities or possess public-law authority.
Independent challenge can produce a real Design Delta without producing a final deal.
A valid negative disposition and exit path are part of a truthful coordination system.
does_not_support: It does not show that Towow or Agent mediation would have improved the project.
It does not show that governance conflict caused termination.
It does not establish the private preferences or complete internal worlds of either party.
competing_explanations: The threshold changes could be ordinary public procurement/governance correction rather than evidence for a new A2A-specific mechanism.
The project may have remained commercially infeasible regardless of governance improvements.
Published consultation records overrepresent views that entered official channels.
design_delta: Add affected-party standing and representation to R/A; signature authority and legitimate challenge rights are distinct.
Compile readiness for public-impact relations must include a legitimacy/standing closure, not only bilateral Mandates.
Do not infer causal failure from a material unresolved issue when the recorded termination cause is different.
Exit can preserve selected rights/knowledge; WITHDRAWN is not equivalent to erasing the relation history.
unknowns: What exact terms would have passed final boards/governments

chronology_preserving_diagnostic.subsequent_observed_change: Threshold resolution changed the same authority/data/scope dimensions; this is chronology-consistent but not a blinded prediction.
chronology_preserving_diagnostic.gate_interpretation: A v0.4-style compile gate should have remained closed before threshold resolution and again where DSAP identified unresolved material details.

cases.title: UK Open Banking
cases.domain: regulated market infrastructure and data sharing
cases.research_role: institutional compilation with technical success and governance failure
cases.case_selection_rationale: The case contains a technical standard, operational rules, large-scale adoption, a governance failure, formal review and transition to a new long-term authority structure.

initial_relation_frame.R: CMA, CMA9 banks, OBIE, third-party providers, consumers/SMEs, FCA, PSR, Treasury and future standards body.
initial_relation_frame.V: API standards, participants, directory, read/write data, service levels, disputes, breaches, suspension/exclusion.
initial_relation_frame.T: Market remedy → standards/governance implementation → participant registration/runtime → monitoring/review → roadmap completion → transition.
initial_relation_frame.A: CMA Order and oversight, OBIE implementation authority, bank/provider obligations, later regulatory allocation to FCA/PSR/Treasury.
initial_relation_frame.E: Conformance, directory status, service monitoring, investigation, governance review and roadmap decisions.
initial_relation_frame.D: Consumer/SME-authorized financial data sharing and payment/data-service rules.
initial_relation_frame.O: Operational participation, roadmap completion, breach/dispute handling, transition to sustainable framework.

powers: develop/operate standards and ecosystem under Order
implement interfaces and comply with rules
future regulatory supervision and smart-data framework
authorize data access/use within the regulated frame; not ecosystem governance principals

timeline.label: CMA remedy mandates an open banking ecosystem
timeline.description: The market remedy creates new participant roles, data-sharing obligations, standards work and an implementation entity under regulatory authority.
timeline.authority_effect: Constitutes institutional authority for a new market relation.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates a mandated formation and implementation path.

timeline.label: Operational governance rules compile roles and runtime procedures
timeline.description: Rules specify registration, roles, standards, service levels, complaints, dispute, breach, suspension, exclusion and amendment.
timeline.authority_effect: Distributes operational and adjudicative powers.
timeline.outcome_effect: Transforms negotiated/mandated design into repeatable participant runtime.

timeline.label: Technical adoption scales
timeline.description: Read/write data-sharing infrastructure is implemented and reaches millions of users and hundreds of providers by the 2022 review.
timeline.authority_effect: Runtime authorization remains grounded in the institutional frame.
timeline.outcome_effect: Shows technical Effect and ecosystem Adoption.

timeline.label: Independent investigation finds governance failures
timeline.description: The investigation identifies failures in corporate governance, conflicts, procurement/value, accounts and HR, with insufficient checks and oversight.
timeline.authority_effect: Challenges the legitimacy/effectiveness of the implementation authority without negating all technical effects.
timeline.outcome_effect: Forces governance remediation while services continue.

timeline.label: Lessons review adds control gates and lifecycle governance
timeline.description: The review concludes the scale/complexity was underestimated and recommends formal review gates, effective governance, stakeholder engagement and clearer monitoring.
timeline.authority_effect: Strengthens sponsor oversight and escalation.
timeline.outcome_effect: Revises institutional compile/readiness semantics.

timeline.label: Roadmap completion and long-term regulatory transition
timeline.description: The technical roadmap is judged substantially complete while the framework transitions from a temporary Order/OBIE model toward long-term FCA/PSR/Treasury authority.
timeline.authority_effect: Reassigns durable authority after initial implementation.
timeline.outcome_effect: Separates implementation completion from final governance settlement.

operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.operation: Banks/providers implemented and operated standardized APIs and directory/governance processes.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.effect: Data-sharing/payment capabilities became available at scale.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.adoption: Millions of users and hundreds of providers used the ecosystem by the 2022 review.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.acceptance: Market adoption was substantial, while governance legitimacy and long-term institutional acceptance remained subject to review and transition.

supports: Technical Effect and Adoption can coexist with institutional governance failure.
Compilation includes standards, registration, dispute, suspension, monitoring and amendment—not only API generation.
A temporary formation authority may need to be replaced by durable regulators after the relation stabilizes.
Governance/authority defects are legitimate reopen triggers even when technical interfaces continue to work.
does_not_support: The case does not test decentralized Agent-to-Agent interaction.
It does not show that a Towow formation process would have prevented governance failures.
User counts do not prove every participant accepted the governance model.
competing_explanations: Open Banking is a state-imposed market remedy; its formation dynamics may not transfer to voluntary non-standard relations.
Reported adoption may be explained by mandate and bank scale rather than governance design.
The lessons reviews are retrospective and institutionally authored.
design_delta: Represent stability as a vector: technical/operational stability cannot average away authority/governance instability.
Define governance debt as a diagnostic when technical runtime is compiled before oversight, dispute and end-state authority are settled; do not create a new aggregate root.
Compile outputs must include amendment, suspension, complaint, dispute, monitoring and institutional succession.
Reopen may target governance subgraphs while leaving safe operational subgraphs running.
unknowns: Long-run distribution of benefits and harms

chronology_preserving_diagnostic.subsequent_observed_change: The 2021–2023 reviews and transition addressed those governance/end-state dimensions.
chronology_preserving_diagnostic.gate_interpretation: Technical compile readiness alone would have produced a false sense of closure; authority/governance stability needed an independent gate.

cases.title: Crossrail / Elizabeth line
cases.case_selection_rationale: Many locally contracted outputs had to become one operational railway. The case exposes the gap between package completion, system integration, assurance and entry into service.

initial_relation_frame.R: Joint sponsors, Crossrail Ltd board/executive, programme partners, 36 main contractors, regulators, operators and assurance bodies.
initial_relation_frame.V: Packages, interfaces, requirements, configuration, testing, commissioning, assurance, operational handover and entry into service.
initial_relation_frame.T: Design/build packages → integrate interfaces → verify/validate → assure/approve → hand over → operate; delay/reset/replan paths.
initial_relation_frame.A: Sponsors set requirements/funding; Crossrail Ltd acts as integrator; contractors own packages; external bodies approve safety/operation.
initial_relation_frame.E: Integrated schedule, interface evidence, verification/validation, independent assurance, operational readiness and regulator approval.
initial_relation_frame.D: Programme controls, risk, schedule, design/configuration and assurance information sharing.
initial_relation_frame.O: Not package completion, but safe integrated railway entry into service and benefits realization.

powers: package delivery; limited interface responsibility under contract design
requirements, interfaces, configuration, verification and integration review
assurance, safety approval and entry-into-service acceptance

timeline.label: System Integration Management Plan establishes integration authority
timeline.description: The plan formally defines Crossrail as systems integrator and creates integration, requirements, interface, configuration, verification and assurance processes.
timeline.authority_effect: Creates explicit integration authority and review structures.
timeline.outcome_effect: Defines how package outputs should become system Effect.

timeline.label: Contract/package design leaves Crossrail holding interface risk
timeline.description: Individual contractors were not required to manage many cross-contract interfaces; the delivery organization retained integration and compensation risk.
timeline.authority_effect: Centralizes system integration responsibility while distributing package execution.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates costly dependency and change-control exposure.

timeline.label: Aspirational plan and optimistic assurance obscure integrated risk
timeline.description: Programme management relied on a plan that did not adequately represent interdependencies, while assurance did not expose the true scale of integration risk.
timeline.authority_effect: Weakens sponsors’ ability to exercise timely intervention authority.
timeline.outcome_effect: Local progress signals fail to prove integrated readiness.

timeline.label: Opening delay reveals failure of end-to-end effect chain
timeline.description: The planned December 2018 opening becomes unattainable; the programme requires a new realistic bottom-up plan and reset.
timeline.authority_effect: Triggers sponsor/governance intervention.
timeline.outcome_effect: Invalidates prior readiness disposition.

timeline.label: Governance and management reset
timeline.description: Independent reviews call for clearer decision rights, transparent risk information, independent assurance, integration accountability and lifecycle-appropriate governance.
timeline.authority_effect: Strengthens oversight and challenge channels.
timeline.outcome_effect: Rebuilds the route from evidence to decisions and operational outcome.

timeline.label: Elizabeth line enters service
timeline.description: The integrated railway reaches operational entry into service after replanning, testing, assurance and staged completion.
timeline.authority_effect: Operational authorities and sponsors accept sufficient readiness.
timeline.outcome_effect: Produces the target-world Effect that package progress alone could not prove.

timeline.label: Interview-based lessons institutionalize lifecycle controls
timeline.description: A 90+ interview review codifies lessons on autonomy, integration accountability, control gates, evolving governance, realistic ranges and assurance.
timeline.authority_effect: Feeds future sponsor authority and project governance.
timeline.outcome_effect: Compiles historical learning into future institutional rules rather than changing the completed railway relation.

operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.operation: Hundreds of design, construction, systems, test and handover operations were performed across packages.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.effect: A safe, integrated railway capable of carrying passengers—not package completion—was the decisive target-world Effect.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.adoption: Operational organizations took over and the Elizabeth line entered service.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.acceptance: Entry into service and sponsor/regulator approvals provide operational acceptance; broader benefit realization is a separate long-run question.

supports: ActionAttempt/package output is not equivalent to integrated system Effect.
A formal integration schema can exist while enacted authority, evidence and incentives fail.
Compile readiness requires end-to-end outcome witnesses and dependency-realistic evidence, not optimistic local progress.
Reopen can be triggered by assurance and governance failure, not only technical version change.
does_not_support: It does not involve autonomous AI Agents or private digital worlds.
It does not prove that a different information architecture alone would have prevented delay.
Retrospective lessons do not identify a single cause of a complex programme failure.
competing_explanations: Fixed-date political/sponsor pressure, commercial incentives, construction uncertainty and organizational culture may independently explain failure.
The integration plan may have been adequate on paper but under-resourced or weakly enforced.
Eventual delivery may reflect extraordinary additional resources rather than superior governance alone.
design_delta: Separate declared schema from enacted schema: authority and witness rules must have observable enforcement, not only documentation.
Operation/Effect/Adoption/Acceptance must be end-to-end and target-world specific.
Compile readiness needs dependency realism, integrated assurance and incentive alignment.
Add assurance failure, reporting opacity and objective drift to Defeater/reopen triggers.
unknowns: Exact counterfactual cost of alternative contract/interface allocation
Causal weights among schedule, culture, incentives and technical complexity

chronology_preserving_diagnostic.subsequent_observed_change: Delay and reviews led to reset, stronger oversight and revised integration/readiness practices.
chronology_preserving_diagnostic.gate_interpretation: A gate based on package progress would pass incorrectly; an end-to-end Effect gate would remain closed.

cases.title: California SGMA intergovernmental coordination
cases.domain: polycentric public governance and shared resource management
cases.research_role: authority-topology and mechanism-choice case with interview-rich evidence
cases.case_selection_rationale: A higher-level mandate requires coordination but deliberately leaves local agencies discretion over how to coordinate. It directly tests whether one mechanism fits all sovereign domains.

initial_relation_frame.R: State mandate, groundwater sustainability agencies, local governments, water users, disadvantaged communities, tribes, private pumpers and basin-level collaborations.
initial_relation_frame.V: GSA/GSP, basin, sustainability objectives, data/models, JPA, MOU, coordination mechanisms and representation.
initial_relation_frame.T: State mandate → local agency formation → mechanism selection → plan coordination → implementation/monitoring and revision.
initial_relation_frame.A: State sets outcomes and deadlines; local agencies retain legal/autonomy interests and choose arrangements; participation and decision authority may differ.
initial_relation_frame.E: Plans, institutional agreements, basin data/models, interviews/observation and coordinated-outcome measures.
initial_relation_frame.D: Local groundwater data/model collection and sharing across agencies and affected users.
initial_relation_frame.O: Multiple mandated coordinated outcomes rather than a single universal organizational form.

powers: mandate sustainability planning and coordinated outcomes
joint planning/decision rights as delegated by members
stakeholder standing and knowledge; participation may not equal formal decision authority
observe, analyze and support; no substantive water authority

timeline.label: SGMA mandates coordinated outcomes but leaves mechanism discretion
timeline.description: The statute creates a common outcome requirement while preserving local choice about organizational form and coordination process.
timeline.authority_effect: State authority defines minimum outcomes; local authority is not erased.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates a family of permissible relation frames rather than one platform workflow.

timeline.label: Local agencies form single and multi-agency GSAs
timeline.description: Basins form different governance structures, including single entities, JPAs, MOUs and multi-level arrangements.
timeline.authority_effect: Creates local and joint authority loci.
timeline.outcome_effect: Produces heterogeneous coordination structures.

timeline.label: Autonomy concerns shape mechanism choice
timeline.description: Empirical analysis finds agencies select mechanisms according to combinations of concerns, with autonomy considerations taking priority.
timeline.authority_effect: Limits how much authority agencies are willing to pool.
timeline.outcome_effect: Mechanism fit depends on concern configuration rather than coordination intensity alone.

timeline.label: Data and model sharing become part of coordination
timeline.description: Agencies must coordinate data, models and planning evidence across basin boundaries while preserving local sources and responsibilities.
timeline.authority_effect: Local evidence sources remain authoritative within a shared planning process.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates shared evidentiary infrastructure without requiring one organization.

timeline.label: Collaborative institutional arrangements vary by required outcome
timeline.description: Across 18 basins, collaborative arrangements are associated with coordinated outcomes, but the effective configuration differs by outcome type.
timeline.authority_effect: Authority topology and rules vary with the mandated outcome.
timeline.outcome_effect: Rejects a universal one-size coordination mechanism.

timeline.label: Peer-reviewed synthesis links configurations to outcomes
timeline.description: Published configurational analysis verifies patterns across basins and identifies collaborative arrangements as important without claiming a single sufficient form.
timeline.authority_effect: Provides external analytic scrutiny.
timeline.outcome_effect: Raises evidence level for mechanism-contingency claims.

operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.operation: Agencies formed governance bodies, negotiated coordination mechanisms, shared data/models and developed basin plans.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.effect: Coordinated planning outputs and institutional arrangements were produced across basins.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.adoption: Local agencies adopted heterogeneous mechanisms under a common mandate.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.acceptance: Formal compliance and coordinated outcomes are observable; full stakeholder legitimacy/acceptance, especially for underrepresented groups, remains uneven and not reducible to plan adoption.

supports: Non-collapsible authority does not imply one decentralized mechanism; autonomy concerns help determine which mechanism is viable.
A common objective can coexist with heterogeneous local relation frames.
Participation/standing and formal decision authority must be represented separately.
Collaborative arrangements matter, but their configuration is outcome-contingent.
does_not_support: It does not test Agent entities, digital Mandates or automated coordination.
It does not establish that all local autonomy claims are normatively justified.
Published configurational relationships are not randomized causal effects.
competing_explanations: Hydrology, prior relationships, basin size and resource conditions may explain both mechanism choice and outcomes.
Top-down deadlines and legal sanctions may drive coordination more than voluntary formation.
Interview and ethnographic interpretation may reflect access and respondent selection.
design_delta: CollapseSafe routing must model autonomy/authority concerns, not only privacy and technical complexity.
Relation Schema should support an institutional frame plus local relation-specific specializations without duplicating all objects.
Add standing/representation coverage to compile readiness and evidence ledgers.
Mechanism choice should be contingent: MOU, JPA, shared standard, central service or local Oracle are alternatives, not maturity levels.
unknowns: Transcript-level evidence not recoded in this runtime
How underrepresented groups altered final decisions
Causal role of facilitation versus pre-existing social capital

pre_outcome_material_gaps: which coordination mechanism fits autonomy concerns
chronology_preserving_diagnostic.subsequent_observed_change: Basins adopted varied structures and collaborative configurations rather than converging on one organizational form.
chronology_preserving_diagnostic.gate_interpretation: A single centralized platform should not be assumed; the correct gate asks whether a chosen mechanism preserves required local authority while satisfying coordinated outcomes.

cases.title: Microsoft acquisition of LinkedIn
cases.case_selection_rationale: A high-value, nontrivial relation was coordinated through a mature legal, board, advisor, disclosure and regulatory frame. It is a negative case against assuming that complexity requires Towow-style open formation.

initial_relation_frame.R: Boards, transaction committee, CEOs, controlling shareholder, advisors, competing bidders, shareholders and regulators.
initial_relation_frame.V: Strategic alternatives, bid, cash/share consideration, exclusivity, antitrust obligations, termination fee, superior proposal, board recommendation and closing.
initial_relation_frame.T: Explore alternatives → bids/diligence → exclusivity/negotiation → board approval → shareholder/regulatory conditions → closing or termination/superior proposal.
initial_relation_frame.A: Board fiduciary authority, committee/advisor process, shareholder/regulatory rights and defined CEO/executive roles.
initial_relation_frame.E: Formal bids, fairness/financial advice, board records, signed merger agreement, votes/approvals and SEC closing filing.
initial_relation_frame.D: Confidential diligence and regulated disclosure; not reconstructed in full from public records.
initial_relation_frame.O: Best value reasonably attainable, definitive agreement, conditions, superior-proposal/termination path and completed merger.

powers: conduct process, negotiate and advise; not final principal
submit/revise proposals; no authority over LinkedIn acceptance

timeline.label: Strategic relationship discussions open multiple alternatives
timeline.description: Executives discuss enhanced commercial relations and possible combinations while LinkedIn also considers standalone and other strategic alternatives.
timeline.authority_effect: Executives can initiate exploration but not bind final acceptance.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates candidate paths inside an established corporate frame.

timeline.label: Board and Transactions Committee formalize decision authority
timeline.description: The board delegates process work to a committee and advisors while retaining fiduciary approval authority.
timeline.authority_effect: Clarifies locus and separation of recommendation from final approval.
timeline.outcome_effect: Makes the search/negotiation process reviewable.

timeline.label: Multiple bidders revise price and form of consideration
timeline.description: Bids and price move through multiple rounds; the central economic parameter changes inside a stable transaction grammar.
timeline.authority_effect: No new authority locus is created by price change.
timeline.outcome_effect: Improves terms without constituting a new institutional frame.

timeline.label: Exclusivity and superior-proposal conditions shape negotiation path
timeline.description: Exclusivity, information rights and later superior-proposal/termination provisions constrain which future negotiation paths remain valid.
timeline.authority_effect: Board authority remains bounded by fiduciary and contract rules.
timeline.outcome_effect: Changes the specific relation trace while staying within mature M&A meta-rules.

timeline.label: Non-price terms define risk, antitrust, termination and support obligations
timeline.description: The relation includes antitrust obligations, termination fees, board-recommendation changes, support agreements and conditions—not only price.
timeline.authority_effect: Distributes risk and future decision authority.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates a precise executable commitment bundle.

timeline.label: Boards approve and parties sign definitive agreement
timeline.description: Authorized boards/parties approve and announce a definitive agreement at $196 per share, subject to conditions.
timeline.authority_effect: Converts negotiation into binding commitments by proper loci.
timeline.outcome_effect: Moves from candidate to committed relation.

timeline.label: Merger closes
timeline.description: The acquisition completes and shares convert under the agreement.
timeline.authority_effect: Regulatory/company filings witness the legal effect.
timeline.outcome_effect: Produces the target-world Effect; long-run value remains separate.

operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.operation: Diligence, bids, negotiation, approvals and legal closing operations were performed.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.effect: LinkedIn became a wholly owned Microsoft subsidiary and shares converted at the agreed consideration.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.adoption: Boards, shareholders/regulators and corporate systems implemented the transaction.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.acceptance: Formal legal/corporate acceptance is evidenced; employee/member/social acceptance and long-run strategic value are not proved.

supports: Complexity alone does not justify an open-ended A2A formation layer.
A mature institutional frame can safely centralize advisors, data rooms and negotiation while preserving board/shareholder/regulatory authority.
Material relation terms can change without changing the higher-level institutional grammar.
CollapseSafe depends on institutional sufficiency, not on whether every term is a simple parameter.
does_not_support: It does not show private worlds were fully represented or that all stakeholders benefited.
It does not prove an Agent could replace boards, advisors or fiduciary judgment.
Public filings cannot reconstruct all rejected alternatives or informal influence.
competing_explanations: The transaction may have succeeded because of concentrated authority and mature law rather than any superior coordination process.
SEC disclosure is ex post and legally curated.
Long-run integration outcomes are outside the coded period.
design_delta: Refine CollapseSafe: a relation can be safely collapsed when a legitimate institutional frame already supplies roles, authority, evidence, dispute, exit and settlement—even if deal terms are complex.
Support two resolution levels using metadata/reference, not new roots: institutional frame and relation-specific version.
Do not route mature transactions to Towow formation merely because many clauses change.
Keep legal Effect distinct from strategic/business Acceptance.

chronology_preserving_diagnostic.subsequent_observed_change: These gaps were resolved through standard committee, board, contract and regulatory procedures.
chronology_preserving_diagnostic.gate_interpretation: Once the definitive agreement and required approvals/witnesses were in place, a deterministic closing workflow was appropriate; persistent intelligent negotiation was unnecessary.
